- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., < 90% of average), consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean, especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00 values), model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- If sentiment is mixed or trending downward, model tends to overcorrect; apply downward bias of 0.5–2% to prevent over-optimism.
- When sentiment is low (≤ 0.33) and price is falling, model often undercorrects — increase forecast slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
